advances: An actual unsampled real-base plateau with one-dimensional fibers.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Each sampled base is extreme in its base square, so the intervals are actual. At $z=(1/2,1/2)$ the admissible barycentric weights have $\lambda_{00}=\lambda_{11}=t$ and $\lambda_{10}=\lambda_{01}=1/2-t$ for $t\in[0,1/2]$. Their intervals are $[t-h,t+h]$, so the real fiber is $[-h,1/2+h]$. The atomic depth at $z$ is $4h$, since a closed halfspace through the center contains at least one vertex of each opposite pair and a generic one contains exactly two.

For $u=1$ the centered margins at the opposite pairs $00,11$ and $10,01$ have sums $1/2$ and $-1/2$, respectively, independently of the tilt $a$. This follows because opposite vertex offsets cancel and their continuous centers sum to $1$ and $0$, respectively, while the mark has continuous coordinate $1/4$. For $u=-1$ the roles reverse. A member of the positive-sum pair has centered margin at least $1/4>h$, so for every $\delta\ge0$ every nonvertical cap includes at least one full interval. For $a=0,u=1$ it includes exactly the $(1,1)$ interval up to null endpoints as long as $\delta\le1/4-h$. At larger displacement a member of the negative-sum pair with centered margin at least $-1/4$ contributes positive additional length, for every tilt and either sign of $u$. The clamping lemma for this fixed mark attains the nonvertical infimum, so these masses give strict depth above $Q$ after the endpoint. This proves the signed radius by the exact scalar law.

For the displayed cap the observed interval projections are $[-h,h]$ and $[1-h,1+h]$, giving exactly the $Q$-plateau $[h,1-h]$. Its left signed margin is $1/4-h$, and its right signed margin is $-3/4+h$. The depth superlevel is already attained at zero displacement, so its nonnegative right-quantile threshold is zero. The mark is the centroid of its real interval, so d90ba05577427854 gives energy $1/2+2h$. Substitution with $M=8h$ into the obstacle gives the formula. Every sampled vertex can be exposed by a base cap containing only itself, so its atomic depth is $Q$ and the infinite-radius convention applies there.

statement:
Take the four actual binary-base interval fibers $K_p=[c_p-h,c_p+h]$, $0<h<1/4$, where $c_{11}=1$ and $c_{00}=c_{10}=c_{01}=0$. Use $\Gamma(u)=|u|$ and the real mark $w=((1/2,1/2),1/4)$ of their canonical hull. Put $Q=2h$. The exact actual depth with displacement $\delta\ge0$ equals $Q$ precisely for $0\le\delta\le1/4-h$, and is greater thereafter. The signed left radius is $1/4-h$, whereas the nonnegative right-quantile displacement threshold for the depth superlevel is zero at the mark. For the cap with $a=0,u=1$ the tail plateau is $[h,1-h]$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ the positive-parameter sublevel obstacle at $w$ is
$$
T_Q(w)=\frac{8h}{\varepsilon^2}\frac{(1/4-h)^2}{1/2+2h}.
$$
At each sampled binary vertex the atomic depth is $Q$ and the sublevel obstacle is infinite.
title: A binary real-base buffer plateau separates the two quantile endpoints
